The Fundamentals
thuh fun-duh-MEN-tulz
noun (essay series, 1910–1915)
From Latin fundamentum, a foundation; the title of a series of essays defending the foundational doctrines of the faith.

Biblical Definition

The Fundamentals were a series of ninety essays published in twelve volumes between 1910 and 1915, funded by two Christian laymen and edited in part by R. A. Torrey, sent freely to ministers, missionaries, and students across the English-speaking world. They were raised up to answer the rising tide of modernism, which under the banner of higher criticism and evolutionary thought was hollowing out the seminaries and pulpits. Against this assault the essays defended the great foundations: the inspiration and inerrancy of the Holy Scriptures, the deity of our Lord Jesus Christ, His virgin birth, His substitutionary atonement for sinners, and His bodily resurrection from the dead. They answered the documentary dismemberment of Moses' books, defended the historicity of the miracles, and held up the gospel of grace against a religion of mere morality. From this great labor the name “fundamentalist” was later taken, denoting one who holds fast these non-negotiable doctrines. Though the essays came from a broad coalition and were not uniformly Reformed in their detail—some leaning dispensational, some Arminian—their witness to the supernatural gospel was clear and courageous. We honor The Fundamentals as a worthy stand for the faith once delivered, a line drawn in a perilous hour, and we receive their core convictions as nothing less than the truth that must be believed and confessed in every age.

Webster 1828 Definition

A 1910–1915 essay series defending the inerrancy of Scripture and the core supernatural doctrines of the faith against modernism.

expand to see more

THE FUNDAMENTALS, noun [Latin fundamentum, a foundation.] A series of ninety essays in twelve volumes, published 1910 to 1915 in defense of the essential Christian doctrines.

Edited in part by R. A. Torrey and distributed freely to ministers worldwide.

Defended the inspiration and inerrancy of Scripture against higher criticism.

Upheld the deity, virgin birth, atoning death, and bodily resurrection of Christ.

“Other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” 1 Corinthians 3:11.

Key Scripture

1Co 3:11 — "For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ."

2Ti 3:16 — "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:"

Isa 7:14 — "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

1Co 15:3 — "For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;"

Modern Corruption

An essay series defending the faith; the corruption it opposed is the very modernism that still denies inerrancy and the supernatural Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the very burden of these essays: the foundational, non-negotiable doctrines of the faith. Modernism, which The Fundamentals arose to answer, dismembered the Scriptures by higher criticism, denied the virgin birth, and recast the atonement and resurrection as symbol—and that unbelief is far from dead in the seminaries and pulpits of our day.

A second danger is the corruption of the word “fundamentalist” itself, which the world now wields as a slur for any narrow or violent zealot. But Scripture says no other foundation can be laid than Jesus Christ, and to hold the fundamentals is simply to hold the gospel. To recover The Fundamentals is to recover both the doctrines they defended and the courage to confess them when the academy mocks.

Hebrew Roots

The title rests on Latin fundamentum, the foundation on which a building is raised.

expand to see more

fundamentum — Latin, a foundation or groundwork.

fundare — Latin, to lay a base, to found.

fundamental — that which is basic and load-bearing.

Applied to the doctrines without which the faith collapses.

Gave the name “fundamentalist” to those who hold them fast.

Usage

"The Fundamentals went out freely to ministers across the world to stem the modernist tide."

"He cited The Fundamentals to show that inerrancy is no recent invention but a defended truth."

"Though a broad coalition wrote The Fundamentals, their witness to the virgin birth and resurrection was one."
